summary: Scene sc_001 (INT. RUINED CATHEDRAL, 0-114960 ms) is shown entirely through on-screen event text EP43:E1 to EP43:E87. Rupert Ashburn orders Alexander Ashburn's arrest; the Royal Guard Captain refuses and salutes Alexander as Duke. A Crown Official then reads a war-office intelligence report that implicates Rupert and Lord Henry Sterling in a leak that led to an ambush and to Alexander's false death declaration. The scene ends with Sterling blocked at the church door by a British Police Constable. Uncertainties: the full contents of the dossiers are not visible, only the quoted passages; the Crown Official's and Guard Captain's names are not given on screen; the chain of who declared Alexander dead and who controlled the estate is stated but not shown; the Dowager Duchess's and Catherine's roles are not explained; and the episode's relation to Episode 42 is not verifiable from the on-screen evidence. Metadata (logline and continuity notes) was treated as non-evidentiary and is not used for any reference or claim.

characters.name: Rupert Ashburn
characters.role: Blond nobleman who claims the title of Lord Rupert Ashburn; accused by the Crown report of treason and of leaking the Duke's position

characters.name: Alexander Ashburn
characters.role: Duke who confronts Rupert, presents the Crown dossiers, and is identified by the Guard Captain as the true Duke

characters.name: Royal Guard Captain
characters.role: Ceremonial guard commander who refuses Rupert's order and salutes Alexander

characters.name: Catherine
characters.role: Bride in the ceremony who reacts in shock and questions Lord Sterling

characters.name: Lord Henry Sterling
characters.role: Seated noble named in the Crown report as a conspirator; attempts to flee the church

characters.name: Dowager Duchess
characters.role: Congregation member who reacts in devastated disbelief to the report

characters.name: Crown Official
characters.role: Crown Military Magistrate who reads the intelligence report and death register aloud

characters.name: British Police Constable
characters.role: Officer who blocks Lord Sterling's exit at the church door

beats.description: Rupert, panicked, calls Alexander a liar and orders the guards to arrest him as an imposter.
Alexander stands composed while Rupert repeats the order; the Guard Captain refuses to obey.
Rupert claims to be the Duke; the Guard Captain salutes Alexander and states that he is the Duke.
Rupert appeals to the congregation, and Alexander answers by calling for the Crown to decide.
Alexander presents a sealed War Office dossier and hands it to the Crown Official to read.
The Crown Official reads an intelligence report stating the ambush was caused by a deliberate leak; Rupert collapses in fear.
Alexander demands the names; the Crown Official names Lord Henry Sterling and Rupert Ashburn.
Alexander confronts Rupert with the betrayal of his men and the theft of his title; Rupert denies it.
The Crown Official opens the sealed document and reads that Alexander was declared dead and his title transferred under false authority.
Rupert blames Lord Sterling for the report; Alexander advances on the altar and turns toward the pews.
Lord Sterling leaves his seat and tries to flee through the church door.
A British Police Constable blocks the doorway, cutting off Sterling's escape as the scene holds until fade to black.

revelations.claim: Alexander says the dossiers were delivered to him under the seal of the Crown.
creates_questions: What do the dossiers contain beyond the passages read aloud?
Who delivered the dossiers and why?

revelations.claim: The Crown Official reads that Alexander's unit was ambushed after his location was compromised, that the leak was deliberate, and that information about the Duke's position was transmitted through British channels.
creates_questions: Who within the British channels passed the information?

revelations.claim: The Crown Official names Lord Henry Sterling and Rupert Ashburn as implicated in the plot.
creates_questions: What penalties or actions will the Crown take against Rupert and Sterling?
What is Sterling's role beyond the report?

revelations.claim: Official death confirmation for Alexander was filed three months after the ambush, he was declared dead, and his estate and title were transferred under false authority.
creates_questions: Who filed the death confirmation and who held the false authority?
Who received Alexander's title and estate after the transfer?

revelations.claim: Rupert claims that Sterling handled the report; this is an accusation made on screen and is not confirmed by any shown evidence.
creates_questions: Did Sterling handle the report, as Rupert alleges?

unresolved_questions.question: What is the full content of the War Office dossiers beyond the quoted passages?
Who within British channels leaked the Duke's position?
Who declared Alexander dead and who held the false authority that transferred his estate and title?
Did Lord Sterling handle the report, as Rupert alleges?
Will Lord Sterling escape or be arrested after the Police Constable blocks his exit?
What is the fate of Rupert, and what did Alexander mean by saying Rupert was told exactly what he needed to hear?
What role do Catherine and the Dowager Duchess play in the wider plot?
